en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-buddhamudrā-samādhi-sūtra*, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han Dynasty.
At that time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain at Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of ten thousand bhikṣus.
The two thousand [monks] were all arhats. At that time, there were four hundred million bodhisattvas, all of whom were like the worthy Maitreya.

Furthermore, bodhisattvas from the eight directions and above and below gradually increased in number beyond measure and incalculable; they all flew to the place where the Buddha was, prostrated themselves with their heads at the Buddha’s feet, rose and circumambulated the Buddha seven times, and then withdrew to sit down. Arranged one above the other in succession, they numbered ten billion layers, beyond further calculation.

Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva possessed the highest talent and was foremost among all; his radiance and wisdom were far superior to those of all other bodhisattvas, such that none could equal him. At that time, the Buddha sat in samādhi.

The outer and inner robes of the Buddha’s body, as well as the light illuminating his seat, all became invisible. Immediately, countless buddha-fields in the eight directions, above, and below were all filled with brilliance. In every one of these buddha-fields, offerings were spontaneously made to the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, arhats, and the assemblies of bhikṣus.
Countless Buddhas from the eight directions, above, and below each dispatched their bodhisattvas to fly to the Buddha’s location, where they sat at the sides of his seat.
All these bodhisattvas assembled, their number being like the sands along the banks of the Ganges River—one sand grain representing one bodhisattva.
In this manner, forty sets of Ganges-sands [of worlds] were all arranged one above the other.
A single bodhisattva sat naturally upon a great lotus flower.
The Buddha withdrew his transformation of the world-system by several thousand li, and once all the bodhisattvas had sat filling it completely.
Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others, along with Śāriputra, immediately stepped forward with palms joined and asked Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva:
"O Benevolent One of supreme talent!"
"The Buddha’s samādhi from earlier is no longer manifest now, and we do not know where he has gone.
We suspect there must be a deeper meaning; we wish to hear it. Mañjuśrī said to Maitreya:
“O virtuous one of great talent!
You shall become a Buddha before long.
As for Śāriputra, you are his disciple; among the disciples of the Buddha, you have attained the path of an Arhat with the most wisdom and fierce talent.”
"Why do you not each sit in meditation with a single mind and investigate how the spiritual power of the Buddha's body functions?

Thereupon, the bodhisattvas, arhats, and others, numbering in the countless millions, all sat with one-pointed minds and searched throughout the eight directions, above and below, across the infinite and boundless buddha-fields. Yet, there was no one capable of knowing the location of the Buddha’s spiritual power within his body.
Maitreya Bodhisattva and others, along with Śāriputra and the rest, again knelt down with palms joined and asked Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva:
"We have sought the spirit of the Buddha’s body with single-minded devotion, yet none among us has been able to know its location."
"I wish to know the explanation for this.
Mañjuśrī said, "All shall sit down comfortably; in a brief moment, they will naturally return."

Hearing that the Buddha had returned to his seat, everyone in the assembly saw the Buddha come back; they were all filled with joy, rose, and prostrated themselves before the Buddha. They also paid homage to Maitreya Bodhisattva and others, as well as Śāriputra and the rest. Then, kneeling with palms joined, they questioned the Buddha:
"During the samādhi just now, the outer and inner robes of the Buddha’s body and spirit were entirely invisible, and we did not know how he moved."

With one mind, we have together sought the divine presence of the Buddha’s body through dhyāna throughout the eight directions, above and below, infinitely and boundlessly; yet we know not at all where the Buddha dwells. We pray that you will let us hear from the Buddha.
The Buddha said:
"The destination reached is profoundly deep; it is not something you can know, for only the Buddhas know it themselves.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
“Samādhi is extremely difficult to encounter; for one to encounter it and hear and know of it is an ineffable joy.
Why is this? Because it is exceedingly difficult to hear.”
The Buddha said:
“If bodhisattvas seek the Way and practice the six pāramitās without fail for a thousand billion kalpas, they may still not attain it;
even when encountering a Buddha’s samādhi, they may still be unable to hear or know the name of that Buddha-samādhi.”

Furthermore, having practiced the six *pāramitās* with diligence and without slackening for three trillion *kalpas*, they may hear the name of a Buddha’s samādhi; yet even upon encountering it, they still do not believe in or incline toward its existence.
Furthermore, even those who practice the six *pāramitās* without fail for seven thousand *koṭis* of *kalpas*, and who hear of the Buddha’s samādhi, may still not believe in its existence.

Furthermore, those who practice the six pāramitās without fail for eight thousand koṭis of nayutas of kalpas, and who hear the name of this Buddha-samādhi, shall then believe in it, turn toward it, and encounter it.

If one who possesses faith and aspiration should encounter [this teaching] at any moment, their heart will be filled with such joy and exultation for a single day and night that it surpasses practicing the six *pāramitās* for three hundred billion *kalpas*.
Why is this? Those who hear and understand this samādhi will subsequently seek the Way and swiftly attain Buddhahood.
The name of this Buddha-samādhi is the Seal of Wisdom of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
When a bodhisattva seeking the Way hears the Wisdom Seal of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, it is a great merit that such a teaching is even heard.
A bodhisattva seeking the Way who desires to become a Buddha must necessarily obtain the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra is the great father and mother of all Buddhas throughout the eight directions, above and below.
Only by attaining the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra can one become a Buddha.
When a bodhisattva seeks the Way, they must accumulate merit and virtue until they are complete before they can hear the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
If a bodhisattva seeking the Way does not obtain the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, they shall not attain Buddhahood.
The Buddha said:

"If there are sons or daughters of good family who, with faith and devotion toward the name of this *Buddhasamādhi Sūtra*, prostrate themselves before it with a compassionate and joyful heart, such persons shall immediately obtain its merit; they shall also obtain merit in future lives. When their life ends, they will be reborn in the heavens as a celestial king; when that life ends, they will descend to be born in the human world and again become a Cakravartin King."

Thus, when their lives end, they will be born in the heavens; when their lives end in the heavens, they will descend to be born into the families of kings and nobles. Circulating thus through the realms of gods and humans, they shall never again fall into the states of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, spirits, or dragons. After incalculable kalpas, they shall all become Buddhas.

If there be anyone who hears the name of this samādhi and harbors even the slightest doubt or lack of faith as large as a hair, that person, at the end of their life, will enter one of the eighteen hells, where they shall be burned and boiled without ever having an opportunity for release.
Only then can those who seek the Way attain it; this is the Unfailing Buddha-nature. Why is this so?
For the *Buddhasamādhi Sūtra* is the essential resolution and the seal of illumination for all Buddhas throughout the eight directions, above and below.
The Buddha said:
"What I have spoken is thus; you all should believe it and not harbor any doubt.
Who shall serve as its witness?"
"Only the bodhisattvas on the shifting sands by the banks of the forty Ganges Rivers are my younger brothers; they alone shall bear witness to this.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva and others, Maitreya Bodhisattva and others, the Arhat Śāriputra and others, as well as all the devas and humans, having heard the sutra, were filled with great joy and rose to pay homage to the Buddha.
The Sutra on the Buddha’s Teaching of the Samādhi of the Buddha-Seal.
